tags.name: SaaS transfers all responsibility
tags.description: Believes that using SaaS means the provider is responsible for everything, including the customer's data and identities.
tags.correct_concept: Data, devices, and accounts/identities are always the customer's responsibility, in every service type.

questions.stem: A manager says: "We use Microsoft 365 (SaaS), so Microsoft is responsible for everything." Which item is still always the company's responsibility?

options.rationale: Data, devices, and accounts/identities remain the customer's responsibility in every service type.
Physical security is always the cloud provider's responsibility.

options.text: Patching the host servers' operating system
options.rationale: Host infrastructure is managed by the provider in SaaS.

options.text: Nothing, because SaaS transfers all responsibility to the provider
options.rationale: Even in SaaS the customer remains responsible for data, devices, and identities.

questions.explanation: Under the shared responsibility model, the customer always owns their information and data, devices, and accounts and identities.
questions.concept_note: Always the customer: information and data, devices, accounts and identities. Always the provider: physical datacenter, network, and hosts.

questions.stem: A company runs a Windows Server virtual machine in Azure (IaaS). Who is responsible for managing and patching the guest operating system?

options.text: Microsoft, because Azure hosts the virtual machine
options.rationale: Hosting the VM does not make Microsoft responsible for the guest OS.
In IaaS the customer manages the guest OS; Microsoft manages the physical hosts and hypervisor.
Responsibility is divided by layer, not split evenly.

options.text: Azure always patches every VM automatically
options.rationale: Patching is not automatic by default.

questions.explanation: In IaaS, the provider is responsible for the physical datacenter, network, and hosts, while the customer manages the operating system.
questions.concept_note: IaaS: customer manages OS, runtime, apps, data. Provider manages physical hosts, network, datacenter.

questions.stem: A company stops buying servers upfront and instead pays monthly for the Azure resources it uses. How does this change its spending?

options.text: It shifts spending from operational expenditure to capital expenditure
Costs become fixed and no longer depend on usage
options.rationale: The consumption-based model ties cost to usage.

options.text: It shifts spending from capital expenditure to operational expenditure
options.rationale: Upfront hardware purchases (CapEx) are replaced by ongoing, usage-based costs (OpEx).

options.text: Costs are unchanged because Azure bills once per year
options.rationale: Azure bills based on usage, typically monthly.

questions.explanation: Cloud shifts spending from CapEx (buying hardware upfront) to OpEx (paying for what you use).
questions.concept_note: CapEx = upfront purchase. OpEx = ongoing spend. Consumption-based = pay for what you use.
